name: Masterclass question in every interview
evidence: Masterclass posts reached 3.3 times the month's median on LinkedIn (6 posts, June to September). Lori Goode's drew 37 comments, the second most of September. The first Masterclass Off Duty cut (Jill Kelly, Oct 28) drew 3,243 LinkedIn impressions and 28 comments, the most of any post Oct 19 to Nov 1. The second Off Duty cut (Chief Johnson, PUMA, Nov 3) drew 138 LinkedIn impressions and 503 Instagram reach.
adherence: Kept in every new question set from September.
next_step: Keep. Masterclass Off Duty episodes are booked to Dec 2.

name: Static news carousel (Industry Movers & Shakers)
evidence: 27% of people who see it click, against 4% for the median post. Reach is about average (0.9 times the month's median). The Oct 30 post drew 71 clicks on 233 impressions (30%). Nov 19: 89 clicks on 442 impressions (20%). On Instagram the format lags: the last three carousels reached 189, 87 and 78 (Nov 20).
adherence: Every two weeks (Oct 16, Oct 30); the Nov 13 slot was skipped and the next ran Nov 19 on LinkedIn and Nov 20 on Instagram, reusing Oct 30's first line and, on Instagram, tagging no one. Booked to Dec 25.
next_step: Keep on LinkedIn for clicks. The Instagram version is the experiment for the week of Nov 30 (tagged collab, new first line).
source: LinkedIn analytics, 5 posts Aug 21 to Oct 30

name: Partners repost with their own words
evidence: Two partner reposts took posts to 8.2 and 7.7 times their organic engagement. Across all September posts the lift was 1.28 times, because most posts had none.
adherence: Most posts still get no partner repost.
next_step: Ask on every post; the nominee repost test (from Oct 26) tries it on nominee posts.

name: Instagram collab posts with the guest or brand
evidence: September's three best Instagram posts were accepted collabs. In October the Top 20 carousel, tagging about 30 brands, reached 4,075 accounts; single-guest reels had a median reach of 198. Tagging the guest's own account goes with it: of the 39 guest reels Oct 6 to Nov 15, the 5 that tagged the guest reached a median 1,001, the 34 that did not 407.
adherence: Standard on honoree and partner posts and extended to guest reels from Oct 26, but the guest's own account was tagged on only 5 of 39 guest reels Oct 6 to Nov 15 and on none of the 9 of Nov 16 to 20.
next_step: Tag and invite the guest's own account on every guest reel (experiment for the week of Nov 30).

name: Soundbite hook opening on reels
evidence: View-through rose from about 34% to 40–44% on hook-format reels. It lifts reach, not how long people stay.
adherence: Standard since July.
next_step: Keep.

name: Newsletter subject lines in Title Case
evidence: Title Case beat lower case on opens. Exception: when the subject line starts with a celebrity's name, lower case won.
adherence: Standard from Sep 1; the exception lives only in notes.
next_step: Write the celebrity-name exception into the newsletter checklist.
source: beehiiv A/B test, Jul 22 to Aug 31

name: Short YouTube ad cut
evidence: The 30-second cut drew 32,881 views at 85.7% average viewed; the 203-second cut drew 8,527 at 34.5%.
adherence: Applies to the next paid flight.
next_step: Lead with short cuts in any future YouTube flight.

name: Links in the LinkedIn first comment, not the post
evidence: Within each post type, no link placement wins: guest interviews with the link in the first comment ran at 1.2 times the month's median, against 2.5 times with the link in the post (4 posts) or with no link (25 posts). Post type drives reach far more than link placement.
adherence: Since Jul 20, 45 of 158 posts put the link in the first comment, 33 in the post and 80 had no link. In October, 23 of 52 had the link in the post.
next_step: Stop policing placement; link every cut to its episode, with a content tag per post so site visits can be read.
source: LinkedIn analytics and comments, May 1 to Oct 24

name: Rewritten LinkedIn bio
evidence: Full months: October drew 185 new followers and 858 page views, against 151 and 678 in September, while impressions rose 8% (58,394 against 53,894). Follows per 1,000 impressions rose from 2.8 to 3.2, and were 3.5 for Oct 19 to Nov 1. There is no control, and the Moment Awards vote ran through October, so part of the gain may come from that. Nov 2 to 15: 60 new followers on 31,069 impressions, 1.9 per 1,000. Nov 16 to 21: 54 new followers on 19,486 impressions, 2.8 per 1,000.
adherence: Live since Sep 30.
next_step: Keep. Recheck follows per 1,000 impressions at the November close.

name: Instagram captions end with "Watch the whole conversation at the link in our bio"
evidence: Link taps over 28 days went from 8 (to Oct 4) to 13 (to Oct 17).
adherence: Rule since Oct 9. The pull now carries full captions: of the 15 guest reels Nov 9 to 20, 14 carry "Watch the full episode at the link in our bio" and Meredith Diehn's (Nov 18) "Full conversation in our link in bio"; none uses the October style guide's "Watch the full conversation through the link in our profile."
next_step: The read still needs Instagram Insights: link taps and site visits from Instagram are not in the Supermetrics pull. Agree one wording with the style guide before the next read.

name: Subscribe prompt moved up the homepage
evidence: Not readable yet: the measure is homepage visits that turn into signups. beehiiv now feeds data/newsletter (pulled Nov 20), but it holds active subscribers by day, not signups by source, and GA4 records no signup event.
adherence: Live since Oct 1.
next_step: Add a signup event in GA4 or a source field in beehiiv, then compare October's signup rate with September's.

name: One Top 20 nominee post a day on LinkedIn, with a repost ask to each nominee
evidence: No post introducing a Top 20 nominee ran on LinkedIn Oct 26 to 30. The Awards posts in that window were vote reminders on Oct 27 (140 impressions) and Oct 30 (143) and the Michelle Crossan-Matos honoree post. Voting closed Oct 30, so the test can no longer run.

source: Weekly briefing, week of Oct 26; LinkedIn analytics

name: Guest reels as Instagram collabs, plus one tagged vote carousel
evidence: Collab status read Nov 12: of the eight single-guest reels Oct 26 to Nov 1, the five accepted collabs reached a median 743 and the three without one 302 (Michelle Crossan-Matos's honoree reel, 772 without a collab, is the exception). Before the test, single-guest reels had a median reach of 198 (Oct 6 to 22). Across October the style guide found 1,634 average views with an accepted collab and 412 without. No tagged vote carousel ran before voting closed Oct 30.
adherence: Five of the eight guest reels of Oct 26 to Nov 1 were accepted collabs. November collab status is not in the data yet.
next_step: Keep on every guest reel. Read November collab status and compare accepted collabs with the rest.
source: Weekly briefing, week of Oct 26; Instagram Insights

name: Recap carousels (documents) on LinkedIn
evidence: The June audit found document carousels drew a 32% median engagement rate, against 10.2% for video and 7.2% for images. Only the news carousel has followed. First reading, Moment Awards (Nov 6): the two non-video recaps on LinkedIn (a winners carousel and a photo gallery on the board) drew 1,494 and 2,235 impressions and 658 and 1,931 clicks, against 1,375 impressions and 39 clicks for the video recap. On Instagram the two carousels reached 3,466 and 3,216, against 1,480 for the reel. The data does not say whether the LinkedIn posts were document posts.
adherence: Used once, for the Moment Awards.
next_step: Test one outside event recap as a document carousel.

name: One LinkedIn guest interview each weekday, brand-side guests Thursday and Friday
evidence: Numbers to beat: 2,790 impressions on Oct 22 to 23 (Thursday and Friday), and 388, the median for non-brand guests Oct 12 to 23, for the two brand-side interviews after seven days. The week before the test, Oct 29 to 30 drew 6,965, with Diana Haussling's honoree post on Thursday and five posts on Friday. Result: Nov 5 to 6 drew 7,567 impressions against 2,790, but those were the Moment Awards days, with three Awards recaps on Nov 6. The one brand-side interview on Thursday or Friday, Catherine Pinkham Berger (Kimberly-Clark, Nov 5), drew 252 against 388.
adherence: Not run as designed: by the post dates in the data, guest interviews went out Mon Nov 2 (two), Tue Nov 3 (four) and Thu Nov 5 (three), with none on Wed Nov 4 or Fri Nov 6.
next_step: Retest in a week without an event, with one guest interview each weekday.
source: Weekly briefing, week of Nov 2; LinkedIn analytics

name: Two Instagram event reels that open on the scene, as collabs with the host
evidence: Numbers to beat: 210, the median guest reel Oct 12 to 25, per reel after seven days (765, the Oct 6 to 9 event reels, is the stretch), and 28-day reach of 28,087 (to Oct 25). Guest reels have since risen to a median 570 (Oct 26 to Nov 1) and 28-day reach to 28,114 (to Nov 1), so 570 is now the tougher bar. Result: the two Awards reels reached 2,863 (Nov 5) and 1,480 (Nov 6), both above 210 and 570, and 28-day reach rose to 31,694 (to Nov 9) from 28,087. The two Awards-night carousels reached more (3,466 and 3,216).
adherence: Both reels came from ATM's own Moment Awards, so there was no outside host to collab with. The Nov 5 reel opened on the night ("Tonight is the night"), the Nov 6 reel on the result. November collab status is not in the data.
next_step: Run it at the next outside event ATM films and read each reel against 570 after seven days.
source: Weekly briefing, week of Nov 2; Instagram Insights

evidence: Numbers to beat: 570 (guest reels Oct 26 to Nov 1); fact hooks had a median of 281 and career-story hooks 475 over Oct 19 to Nov 1. Nov 2 to 15, without the split: four career-moment hooks reached a median 734 (Justin Breton 2,144, Jessica Padula 828, Brittany Slattery 640, Colleen Dawe 253) and three number hooks 377 (Catherine Berger 769, Charlotte Owen 377, Amanda Farrand 288). Rerun Nov 18 to 20 (all under seven days old): none of the five guest reels opened on a number or fact from the interview. Two opened on a career or family moment (Justin Thomas-Copeland 211, Joe Ligé 143), two on a line (Keri Richardson 157, Brian Cordes 288) and one on a scene (Meredith Diehn 608). The one fact hook nearby, Matt Strauss ("First to air the Super Bowl", Nov 17), reached 293.

source: Weekly briefing, week of Nov 9; Instagram Insights
